evidence.quote: I expect that economic conditions will support the first rate increase later this year.
My view is that, if the economy continues on its expected path, it will be appropriate for a time to increase rates fairly gradually.
But the unemployment rate probably understates the amount of slack still remaining in the labor market.
The biggest risk of tightening too early or too fast is that the economy may weaken more than expected, forcing the central bank to reverse course.
we should look for a little more proof than usual that labor markets are tightening or other supply-side constraints are binding.
These low current readings are partly a consequence of two transient shocks--the dramatic decline in oil prices and the effect of the appreciation of the dollar on import prices.

parsed.rationale: Although the speaker expects liftoff later this year, the emphasis is on a gradual pace, on remaining labor-market slack, and on wanting extra proof before removing accommodation to allow supply-side healing. He also weights the risks of tightening too early more heavily than overheating, which nets to a moderately dovish signal.
